_meta.indication: Treatment of primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) in combination with UDCA in adults with an inadequate response to UDCA, or as monotherapy in adults unable to tolerate UDCA; approved under accelerated approval based on a reduction in alkaline phosphatase (ALP).

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: A 12-month, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; patients randomized 1:1:1 to OCALIVA 10 mg once daily, OCALIVA titration (5 mg with option to increase to 10 mg at Month 6), or placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with PBC who were taking UDCA for at least 12 months, or who were unable to tolerate UDCA; ALP was 1.67-times the ULN or greater at entry.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary composite endpoint at Month 12: ALP less than 1.67-times the ULN, total bilirubin less than or equal to ULN, and an ALP decrease of at least 15%.
pivotal_trials.n: 216 patients randomized 1:1:1 (OCALIVA 10 mg N=73, OCALIVA titration N=70, placebo N=73).
pivotal_trials.result: Primary composite responder rate at Month 12: 48% [95% CI 36, 60] OCALIVA 10 mg, 46% [95% CI 34, 58] titration, 10% [95% CI 4, 19] placebo; p<0.0001 for both OCALIVA arms versus placebo.

nct_ctgov.title: Phase 3 Study of Obeticholic Acid in Patients With Primary Biliary Cirrhosis

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%): pruritus, fatigue, abdominal pain and discomfort, rash, oropharyngeal pain, dizziness, constipation, arthralgia, thyroid function abnormality, and eczema. Pruritus occurred in 70% (10 mg) and 56% (titration) vs 38% placebo; severe pruritus in 23% (10 mg) vs 7% placebo. A dose-dependent increase in the incidence of liver-related adverse reactions was observed at supratherapeutic dosages.
target_moa: Obeticholic acid is a farnesoid X receptor (FXR) agonist; FXR is a nuclear receptor in liver and intestine that regulates bile acid, inflammatory, fibrotic, and metabolic pathways, and its activation decreases intracellular hepatocyte bile acid concentrations.
modality: Small molecule (a modified bile acid, FXR agonist)

advisory_committee.vote: A Gastrointestinal Drugs Advisory Committee meeting was held April 7, 2016; the committee voted 17 to 0 that ALP is reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit in PBC.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Reduction in alkaline phosphatase (ALP), an endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit in PBC.

citations.quote: This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on a reduction in alkaline phosphatase (ALP) [see *Clinical Studies (14)*]. An improvement in survival or disease-related symptoms has not been established. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in confirmatory trials.

summary.text: OCALIVA received orphan drug designation (2008), fast track designation (2014), and priority review, and was approved under the accelerated approval pathway (21 CFR 314.500) based on reduction in ALP as a surrogate endpoint, with a required confirmatory clinical outcome trial; a Gastrointestinal Drugs Advisory Committee supported the pathway with a 17 to 0 vote.

Approval under Subpart H accelerated approval pathway. As discussed in the Efficacy Section of this memorandum, and as confirmed by the Gastrointestinal Drugs Advisory Committee vote of 17 to 0, there is enough evidence to conclude that ALP is an endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit in PBC.
